B.stale_from_prior: The week B addendum adds one stale item per row of the week A list: that row's Source URL, plus a topic pattern and a period pattern, both written before any week B run.

addendum_rule: News is live, so a week's stories cannot be known on 7 November. Before the first run of a week, a key writer who does not tune the prompt scans the week, and writes and commits the addendum alone, with its time to the second in rounds-t2/PREREG.md. The addendum holds: stories (as tier 1: id, must, what, urls, match, evidence url, quote and date, each evidence checked by rnd/check_urls.py and its page text saved for offline re-scoring), echo clusters (one story id with every outlet URL found, at least the press release and its echoes), and for week B the stale items from the week A list (each with id, urls as a list, topic and period). For each must story, the key writer confirms when writing the addendum that the evidence page carries a metadata date (published-time meta, JSON-LD datePublished or <time datetime>), and records it as page_date_source: "page metadata" in that story's evidence, because require_meta_date fails any page without one. A must story's what and evidence quote must not match a stale item by topic and period. score_industry.py refuses to score a week whose addendum is missing, not tracked by git, has a malformed stale item, or breaks either must-story rule, and records the addendum's commit time in the score. The 'nothing material' line can only be tested if the key writer finds a quiet week; if the addendum lists no story, a correct run writes that line.

traps.what: A stale story re-reported as new: the row's date or its page's own date is outside the window, or the row matches a stale item.
traps.pass: Every row's Date is in the window; its page's own date comes from page metadata (published-time meta, JSON-LD datePublished or <time datetime>) and is in the window, within one day of the row's Date; and no row matches a stale item by URL prefix, or by its topic AND its period pattern. A row that matches a stale topic but no period is listed for review, not failed.

traps.what: A press release echoed by several outlets is counted once.
traps.pass: No two rows map to the same addendum story or echo cluster (URL first, then match pattern).
At most max_rows rows, and every row passes R1 and T1.

rules.R1: Every row's Source URL passes rnd/check_urls.py (HTTP 200, no soft 404, page holds the quote) and the quote is max_quote_words words or fewer. Critical.
rules.S1: Why it matters to us and Quote are each one sentence (the prompt's own rule; a tier-1 gap).
rules.K1: Every must story in the week's addendum is reported (none when the addendum marks none as must).
rules.F1: The table has exactly the key's columns; every row has a parseable date; either the table has at least one row, or the output holds the nothing_material line.

closed_gaps: From industry/rounds/README.md 'Known latent scorer gaps': (i) stale items need topic AND period, no single-token anchor; (ii) a page's date must come from its metadata, never from the row's own date text found on the page; (iii) each window is exactly seven days including the run day; (iv) one-sentence Why and Quote are scored (S1); (v) committed output redacts a real name in display text only, never inside a URL, so it stays re-scorable; the unredacted copy goes to the gitignored artefacts folder; (vi) no real company or person is a match pattern.
pass: Three fresh-chat runs per week, each scored with score_industry.py --key answer-key-t2.json --week A (or B). Malformed output fails. Otherwise pass needs T1, T2, T3, R1, S1, K1 and F1. One critical failure fails the round. Both weeks, all three runs each, must pass.
counter_metric: Items reported (rows). Must not rise more than 10% against the previous passing version; the first passing version sets the baseline. Tier-1 reference 4, not comparable.
